newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money market rates remain pinned at highs.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money market rates remain pinned at highs.

text.p: Dutch money market rates remained pinned at high levels on Tuesday and traders said they did not expect a significant drop soon.
"I expect rates to stay at these levels for a while," one dealer said.
Call rates have been hovering at fairly high levels for weeks and have stuck at around 2.81 percent bid for the last three days. Call money was quoted at 2.81 to 2.87 percent bid.
Dealers said that until recently the finance ministry's Dutch Treasury Certificate programmes had served as a barrier to rates coming down.

But they said the DTC programmes could no longer be considered a reason for keeping rates high, as the finance ministry had now closed its January programme and fixed the payment date of its February and March DTC programmes for January 15.
"The ministry got in a tidy amount of money under its January DTC programme this morning, so they closed it," one dealer said.
"Theoretically, rates ought to go down now," another said.
The persistent high level of the money market rates was blamed on a continuing liquidity shortage.
"There have been more tax payments than we expected, which also keeps rates up," one dealer said.
Dealers said there had been reasonable volume in one-month and longer-dated deposits, which is usual at this time of the year, due to end-of-year window-dressing.
The guilder was pegged at 112.22 guilders per 100 marks.
